# Job Chapter 42 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 432r

---

**42:1** And-answered [vaya'an] Iyyov [את] YHWH and-said: **42:2** "I-know [yada'ti] that you-can-do [tukhal] all-things [kol], and-no purpose [mezimmah] of-yours can-be-thwarted [lo yibatser mimekha].

**42:3** 'Who [is] this who-hides [ma'alim] counsel [etsah] without knowledge [beli-da'at]?' Therefore I-have-uttered [higgadti] [what] I-did-not understand [ve-lo avin], things-too-wonderful [nifla'ot] for-me [mimmenni], [which] I-did-not know [ve-lo eda].

**42:4** 'Hear [shema] now, and-I will-speak [adabber]; I-will-ask-you [eshalkha] and-make-known [hodi'eni] to-me.'

**42:5** By-the-hearing of-the-ear [le-shema-ozen] I-had-heard-of-you [shamatikha], but-now [ve-attah] my-eye [eini] sees-you [ra'atka]. **42:6** Therefore I-despise [em'as] and-I-repent [ve-nichamti] upon dust [al-afar] and-ashes [va-efer]."

**42:7** And-it-was after YHWH spoke [dibber] [את] these-words [ha-devarim ha-elleh] to Iyyov, and-said YHWH to Eliphaz the-Temanite, "My-anger [chori appi] has-burned [charah] against-you and-against your-two friends [shnei re'eikha], for you-did-not speak [lo dibbartem] to-me [elai] what-is-right [nekhonah] as-my-servant [ke-avdi] Iyyov [did].

**42:8** And-now, take [qechu] for-yourselves seven bulls [parim] and-seven rams [eilim] and-go [lekhu] to my-servant [avdi] Iyyov, and-offer-up [ve-ha'alitem] a-burnt-offering [olah] for-yourselves [ba'adekhem]; and-Iyyov my-servant [avdi] will-pray [yitpallel] for-you [aleikhem], for his-face [panav] only [im-ki] I-will-accept [essa], so-as-not to-deal [le-vilti asot] with-you [immakhem] according-to-your-folly [nevalah]; for you-did-not speak [lo dibbartem] to-me [elai] what-is-right [nekhonah] as-my-servant [ke-avdi] Iyyov."

**42:9** And-went [vayelekhu] Eliphaz the-Temanite and-Bildad the-Shuhite [and] Tsophar the-Naamathite, and-they-did [vaya'asu] as YHWH spoke [dibber] to-them; and-YHWH accepted [vayissa] the-face [penei] of-Iyyov.

**42:10** And-YHWH turned [shav] the-captivity [shevit] of-Iyyov when-he-prayed [be-hitpallelo] for his-friends [re'ehu]; and-YHWH added [vayosef] [את] all that [was] to-Iyyov doubled [le-mishneh].

**42:11** And-came [vayavo'u] to-him all his-brothers [echav] and-all his-sisters [achyotav] and-all who-had-known-him [yode'av] before [le-fanim], and-they-ate [vayokhelu] with-him bread [lechem] in-his-house [be-veito]; and-they-showed-sympathy [vayyanudu] to-him and-comforted-him [vayenachamu] over all the-evil [ha-ra'ah] that YHWH had-brought [hevi] upon-him; and-they-gave [vayyittenu] to-him each-one [ish] a-qesitah [qesitah echad] and-each-one [ish] a-ring [nezem] of-gold [zahav] one [echad].

**42:12** And-YHWH blessed [berakh] [את] the-latter-days [acharit] of-Iyyov more-than [me-reshito] his-beginning [reshito]; and-he-had [vayehi] fourteen-thousand [arba'ah-asar elef] sheep [tson], and-six-thousand [sheshet alafim] camels, and-a-thousand [elef] yoke [tsemed] of-oxen [baqar], and-a-thousand [elef] female-donkeys [atonot].

**42:13** And-he-had [vayehi] seven [shiv'anah] sons [banim] and-three [shalosh] daughters [banot]. **42:14** And-he-called [vayiqra] the-name of-the-first [ha-rishonah] Yemimah [Jemimah], and-the-name of-the-second [ha-shenit] Qetsi'ah [Keziah], and-the-name of-the-third [ha-shelishit] Qeren-Happukh [Keren-Happuch].

**42:15** And-were-not found [ve-lo nimtse'u] women [nashim] as-beautiful [yafot] as-the-daughters of-Iyyov in-all the-land [be-khol ha-arets]; and-gave [vayyitten] to-them their-father [avihem] an-inheritance [nachalah] among [be-tokh] their-brothers [acheihem].

**42:16** And-lived [vayechi] Iyyov after this [acharei-zot] a-hundred and-forty [me'ah ve-arba'im] years [shanah]; and-he-saw [vayar] [את] his-sons [banav] and [את] his-sons' sons [benei-vanav], four generations [arba'ah dorot]. **42:17** And-died [vayamat] Iyyov, old [zaqen] and-full of-days [u-seva yamim].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.5 — "hearing of the ear… my eye sees you":** This is the theological center of the entire book. The contrast is between *shema* (hearing/report) and *ra'ah* (seeing/experiencing). Job's knowledge of God has moved from secondhand to firsthand. The encounter itself — not any explanation — is what transforms him.

**v.6 — "I despise and repent":** Hebrew *em'as ve-nichamti al-afar va-efer*. The verb *em'as* ("I reject/despise") has no stated object — what does Job despise? Possibilities: himself, his words, his complaint, his dust-and-ashes condition. The ambiguity may be intentional. *Nichamti* can mean "repent," "relent," "be comforted," or "change one's mind." The traditional "I repent in dust and ashes" is only one possible reading.

**v.7 — "you did not speak to me what is right as my servant Job":** Hebrew *lo dibbartem elai nekhonah ke-avdi Iyyov*. This is the divine verdict that overturns the entire dialogue. The three friends who defended God are rebuked; Job who challenged God is vindicated. The word *nekhonah* means "established/correct/right." God calls Job *avdi* ("my servant") four times in vv.7-8 — the same title used in the prologue.

**v.15 — "inheritance among their brothers":** Job's daughters receive an inheritance alongside their brothers — highly unusual in the ancient Near East and a sign of radical restoration.

*— EMET*
